intent: "What is queued to go out, to whom, and when?" — by person, campaign, sender, or everything

input_schema.title: message.status input
input_schema.description: One send an earlier work item of this campaign made, read by the reference the provider gave it. The caller names the work item; the runtime supplies the reference it kept, so no caller can name one.

send.description: The work item of this campaign whose send is read: a `message.send` or a `social_invitation.send` that succeeded with a reference.
The send `args.send` names, composed by the runtime from the attempt that made it: never written by a caller.

work_item.description: The work item that made the send, as `args.send` names it.

reference.description: The provider's reference for the send, as that work item's succeeded attempt returned it under `external_ids.send`.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

state.description: `queued`: the provider holds the send and it has not gone yet. `sent`: it went. `cancelled`: it was cancelled before it went. `failed`: the provider took it and it did not go. `unknown`: the provider attempted the send and lost track of it, so it may have gone. The last four are final.

cancelable.description: Whether the send can still be cancelled by its reference: only a queued send the provider is not already sending.

accepted_for.description: The moment the provider holds the send for, in UTC, or null where it holds it for none.

sent_at.description: When the send went, in UTC, or null where it has not gone or the provider gives no moment known to be UTC.

message_id.description: The provider's identifier for the message that went, or null where none went or it gives none.

rendered_subject.description: The subject as it went, or null where the provider gives none.

rendered_body.description: The body as it went, the provider's signature and tracking applied, or null where the provider gives none.

failure_reason.description: The provider's own sentence for why a failed send did not go, or null where it gives none.

failure_code.description: The provider's own code for a failure, as it gives it and uninterpreted, or null where it gives none.

cancelled_at.description: When the send was cancelled, in UTC, or null where it was not or the provider gives no moment.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no send under the reference, or not one this account may see. Nothing was read.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read this account's sends.
The provider refused the call for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: The send read is the one the runtime names under `send.reference`; the plugin reads by nothing the caller wrote.
A send the provider is already sending is `queued` and not `cancelable`; a state the provider adds later that still holds the send is `queued`.
A send the provider attempted and lost track of is `unknown`, final and not `cancelable`: it may have gone, and is never told as `failed`, which says it did not.
A send that went is `sent` whether or not the provider names the moment or the message; the runtime says it went once, in the journal, and never rewrites the send's own result.
An answer larger than the plugin may read from a program fails `provider_answer_too_large` as permanent: asking again would cut it at the same place.
